foundingStory:
Hult Prize @ UC Davis began with one student. As founder and campus director, they built the chapter from the ground up — recruiting its first members, assembling an executive board, and earning faculty support on the way to official university organizational recognition.

From there, the chapter took on the work of running UC Davis's own official Hult Prize OnCampus competition: recruiting judges from both academia and industry, and managing everything from event logistics and communications to judging and team coordination.

More than 20 teams have since participated through the chapter and its broader course ecosystem, with two advancing to the Hult Prize National Competition — see the full numbers on [our Impact section →](index.html#impact).

eng108Section: One of the chapter's most significant achievements has been its long-term collaboration with ENG 108 at UC Davis. That partnership has been used to expose far more students to entrepreneurship and startup development than the chapter could reach on its own — substantially expanding participation in the competition each year.
legacySection: When the chapter's founder transferred away from UC Davis, Hult Prize @ UC Davis kept going. The organization continued operating under its executive board — evidence that what was built here was designed to be sustainable, run by a team rather than dependent on any one person.
